title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Backend** | The code that connects ImGui to a platform (input, window, clock: `imgui_impl_win32`) and a renderer (drawing: `imgui_impl_dx11`). ImGui itself does neither. (1.02) |
| **Begin / End** | The pair that opens and closes a window. `End` must always be called, even when `Begin` returns false. (1.04) |
| **BeginChild** | A scrolling region inside a window with its own size, border and scroll position. (3.02) |
| **Clipper** | `ImGuiListClipper`: tells you which rows of a long list are visible so you submit only those. (3.02) |
| **Collapsing header** | A full-width header that shows or hides the widgets after it, without indenting them. (3.05) |
| **Command list** | A list of draw commands (vertices, indices, texture, clip rectangle) that the renderer backend turns into GPU draw calls. (1.03) |
| **Context** | `ImGuiContext`: all of ImGui's state. Created with `CreateContext`, destroyed with `DestroyContext`. (1.02) |
| **Dear ImGui** | A C++ immediate-mode GUI library for tools and debug UI, by Omar Cornut. (1.01) |
| **Docking** | The docking-branch feature that lets windows be docked into each other as tabs and splits, arranged by a dock space. (4.04) |
| **Dock space** | An area that windows can be docked into; `DockSpaceOverViewport` makes the whole main window one. (4.04) |
| **DockBuilder** | The internal API for building a default dock layout in code on first run. (4.04) |
| **Drag and drop source / target** | A widget that starts a drag with a typed payload, and a widget that accepts payloads of a matching type. (4.03) |
| **Draw data** | `ImDrawData`: everything ImGui wants drawn this frame, produced by `Render`. (1.03) |
| **Draw list** | `ImDrawList`: the list of shapes a window draws, which you can add lines, rectangles, circles and text to yourself. (1.03, 5.01) |
| **Font atlas** | One texture holding every glyph of every loaded font at its size. (4.05) |
| **Frame** | One pass of `NewFrame`, your UI code, `Render` and drawing the draw data. ImGui rebuilds the UI every frame. (1.03) |
| **Hot, active, focused** | The widget under the mouse, the widget being pressed or dragged, and the widget receiving keyboard input. (1.01) |
| **ID** | The number ImGui uses to tell widgets apart, hashed from the label and the ID stack. (1.05) |
| **ID stack** | `PushID` / `PopID`: scopes that make the same label unique in different places, such as rows of a list. (1.05) |
| **Immediate mode** | A GUI style where the program describes the UI from its own data every frame, and the library keeps almost no widget objects. (1.01) |
| **ini file** | `imgui.ini`: where ImGui saves window positions, sizes, docking and table settings, and where your own settings handlers can save more. (4.06) |
| **`##` and `###`** | In a label, `##` hides what follows but keeps it in the ID; `###` makes only what follows the ID, so the visible text can change. (1.05) |
| **Item** | The last widget submitted; `IsItemHovered`, `IsItemActive`, `IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit` and friends ask about it. (1.04) |
| **Metrics window** | `ShowMetricsWindow`: ImGui's own debug view of windows, draw lists and IDs. (1.06) |
| **Modal** | A popup that blocks the rest of the UI until it is closed, such as a confirmation dialog. (4.02) |
| **Multiple viewports** | The feature that lets ImGui windows leave the main window and become real OS windows. (4.04) |
| **Payload** | The typed data carried by a drag and drop. (4.03) |
| **Popup** | A window opened with `OpenPopup` and shown with `BeginPopup`, closing when you click elsewhere. (4.02) |
| **Retained mode** | A GUI style where the library keeps a tree of widget objects that the program creates, changes and destroys. (1.01) |
| **Selectable** | A widget that can be highlighted as selected, used for lists and menus. (2.03) |
| **Self time** | In a profiler, a zone's total time minus the time spent in its child zones. (6.02) |
| **Settings handler** | `ImGuiSettingsHandler`: your own section in the ini file, read and written by callbacks. (4.06) |
| **Style** | `ImGuiStyle`: sizes, roundings and colours for every widget. (4.05) |
| **Table** | `BeginTable`: columns with headers, resizing, reordering, sorting and scrolling. (3.03) |
| **Text filter** | `ImGuiTextFilter`: a box where the user types comma-separated terms, with `-` for exclusions, to filter lines. (5.02) |
| **Tree node** | A widget that expands to show indented children; `TreePop` closes its scope. (3.04) |
| **Undo step** | One user action recorded as the change needed to undo and redo it; a whole drag is one step. (5.04) |
| **`WantCaptureMouse` / `WantCaptureKeyboard`** | Flags ImGui sets when it is using the mouse or keyboard, so the game should ignore them. (2.05) |
| **Zone** | In a profiler, a named span of time marked by a begin and an end event. (6.02) |
